scope: All72 Linux screenshot candidates. Exact static screenshot acceptance; no baseline or site source edits.

coverage.method: Whole-image inheritance only for exact approved hashes. Other images compared by full-width row hashes against previously inspected candidates or committed baseline; only pixel-identical rows carry forward, including vertically shifted runs. Every changed interval inspected with80px surrounding context in unscaled generated crops; long desktop composites may be display-resized. Full-page overviews checked flow. Prior held images receive explicit fresh overlap-region review. Gray headers and strip seams are inspection artifacts. No automatic acceptance of changed pixels.

resolvedFindings.title: Keep floating controls clear of mobile prose

affectedImages.evidence: Chat sits in the clear right-hand gap beside the Hello, I’m Terry heading, above the opening paragraph; biography prose is unobscured.
Chat sits beside Website packages in the heading gap. Editing/ownership, outside-cost and optional-care wording is unobscured.
Chat sits in the gap below/right of the AssetRounds title and product-site line, above the paragraph. Portfolio description is unobscured.
Back-to-top sits in the gap after the price/terms paragraph before the example label. Chat sits right of EXAMPLE WEBSITE BRIEF and above its body text; neither control covers captured prose.

limits: Acceptance covers supplied screenshot states and exact hashes only, not every route, scroll position, zoom, motion or interactive state.
No per-route visual/accessibility rating or overall quality total is assigned. Content correctness and interaction/accessibility need separate evidence.

Nine committed-baseline matches are treated as already approved;19 match explicit prior independent acceptances. Unchanged pixels within the44 manual reviews inherit prior inspection; changed pixels and transition boundaries were inspected.
Captures are bound to the stated commit/run. Subsequent changes require independent evidence of unchanged pixels.
